thread:
maria: Heads-up — canary @dedicated pool shows a ~28% token/sec drop starting at 09:07 UTC after the 2026-03-02 rollout.
maria: Heartbeat graphs: token/s went from ~230k -> ~165k, p95 latency +40ms. No error rate spike.
kevin: ack. Any obvious change in batch sizes or coalesce counts? logs?
sanjay: pulling runtime logs now. early look: a lot more kernel-fallback paths triggered and memcopy time per-op spiked.
sanjay: snippet from runtime debug (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-02T09:07:12Z] kernel_choice=mkldnn -> fallback memcpy
[2026-03-02T09:07:12Z] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.21 hit_rate=0.79
[2026-03-02T09:07:12Z] batch_size=6 avg_coalesce_wait_ms=24
[2026-03-02T09:07:12Z] memcpy_us=4120  // previously ~800
```
linda: that coincides with my rollout that bumped scheduler prefetch stride from 4 -> 8 (PR #3421). I can roll back if we want.
kevin: interesting — increasing prefetch stride should reduce cold misses, not increase them. maybe it changed the interleaving and caused more evictions? or changed kernel affinity choices when seq-len distribution changed.
maria: perf-ci flagged this in nightly too: see @perf-ci report.
perf-ci: regression detected: tokens/sec -27.9% relative to baseline (ref=main@c1a2b3). CI profile shows memcopy% of CPU time 3% -> 18% on worker-3.
kevin: can we reproduce locally by toggling prefetch stride to 8 and running the microbench harness? anyone tried?
sanjay: yes, local microbench with the exact traffic shape reproduced ~25% drop. Bisect points to commit 1b4f7a5 (scheduler: prefetch stride + coalesce timing tweak).
maria: do we have a cheap mitigation? maybe force kernel_selection to prefer copyless path via `--kernel-hint=prefer-inplace` while we revert scheduler tweak.
kevin: good idea. Also we could temporarily lower prefetch_stride back to 4 via runtime flag to unstick rollout (no full revert) — faster rollback path.
linda: i'll hold the rollout and flip the feature flag for the canary now.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-02T09:42:00 started by linda — feature_flag.scheduler_prefetch_stride=4 -> success
maria: after rollback to stride=4 token/s recovered to within 3% of baseline on canary.
sanjay: added detailed traces to the bisect ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/RI-8672 — includes perf traces, kernel decision logs, kv miss histograms.
kevin: follow-up actions: 1) deeper profiling of memcopy (which backend triggers it) 2) unit test for stride-change interaction with kv eviction 3) revert PR or add safety check to avoid kernel fallback on high-memcopy paths.
maria: agreed. i'll open the rollback PR and assign to @linda for final sign-off. thanks team :thumbsup:
linda: will do. good catch everyone.
